extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of metaphysics and philosophy (Schopenhauer scholars, general philosophical readership)
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter-length philosophical treatment arguing that the will (the thing-in-itself), not the intellect, is indestructible; examines death, generation, individuality, and the distinction between phenomenon and thing-in-itself. Presents metaphysical arguments about immortality, the role of time, and the nature of consciousness.
